title: Ethiopian Berbere Mayonnaise
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Berbere Mayonnaise — commercial or home-made mayonnaise mixed with berbere, a pinch of mitmita, and lemon. The modern condiment that bridges Ethiopian spice tradition with international café culture — used in sandwiches, burgers, and alongside fried foods.
longDesc: Berbere mayo is what Ethiopian cafés serve with their craft burgers, their fried fish sandwiches, and their chips — the familiar mayo format given an unmistakably Ethiopian character by berbere and mitmita.
steps: Taste and adjust berbere and lemon.
chefTips: Start with 1 tsp berbere and taste — berbere varies significantly in heat between batches.
The mitmita adds a finishing heat punch.
commonMistakes: Not tasting before serving — berbere batches vary.
cookingScience: The mayonnaise's emulsified fat dissolves the fat-soluble carotenoids and capsaicinoids from the berbere — producing a uniformly spiced, richly coloured condiment where the berbere flavour is distributed throughout every portion.
sustainabilityTips: Use home-made mayonnaise for the most sustainable version.
culturalNote: Berbere mayo is the symbol of the new Ethiopian café generation — the young Ethiopian who has grown up eating injera and Doro Wat but also burgers and café food, and who brings the berbere tradition to every format they engage with.
